blogs.title: When Headache Meets Hyponatremia: Unmasking SIADH as a Hidden Complication of Acute Neuro-Behçet's
blogs.description: This post explores the rare but critical intersection of acute neurological Behçet's disease (neuro-BD) and Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH). We analyze how CNS inflammation in neuro-BD can trigger dysregulated ADH release, potentially mediated by IL-6 pathways, and discuss why persistent hiccups and rhabdomyolysis should raise immediate red flags for severe hyponatremia in patients presenting with fever and headache.

blogs.title: The Normal MRI Trap: Diagnosing Acute Neuro-Behçet's Without Parenchymal Lesions
blogs.description: Acute neuro-Behçet's is classically associated with brainstem lesions, yet this case demonstrates a presentation with aseptic meningitis and a completely normal brain MRI. We discuss the diagnostic tension when imaging fails to show pathology, emphasizing the reliance on clinical criteria (oral/genital ulcers, skin lesions) and CSF analysis (lymphocytic pleocytosis) to distinguish acute neuro-BD from viral encephalitis or malignancy in the early phases.

blogs.title: Colchicine Monotherapy in Acute Neuro-Behçet's: A Paradigm Shift or a Fluke?
blogs.description: Standard guidelines recommend high-dose corticosteroids and immunosuppressants for acute neuro-BD. This case challenges that dogma by documenting complete resolution of mucocutaneous, neurological, and endocrine symptoms using colchicine monotherapy alone. We examine the mechanisms of colchicine in suppressing IL-1β and IL-6, review existing literature suggesting its inefficacy in parenchymal disease versus its potential utility in meningoencephalitic presentations, and debate whether this represents a new therapeutic avenue or a spontaneous remission outlier.

blogs.title: Beyond the Pinprick: Navigating the Diagnostic Maze When Genital Ulcers Are Absent at Onset
blogs.description: Diagnosing Behçet's is notoriously difficult when classic mucocutaneous features appear sequentially rather than simultaneously. This post details the diagnostic odyssey where genital ulcers—the hallmark specific sign—appeared days after admission. We explore strategies for managing 'probable' Behçet's in the ED before definitive criteria are met, discussing the role of HLA-B51 (and its limitations), the interpretation of non-specific markers like sIL-2R, and how to avoid over-testing while ruling out mimics like sarcoidosis and lymphoma.

blogs.title: Persistent Hiccups and Rhabdomyolysis: The Underappreciated Signs of Severe Hyponatremia in Neuro-Inflammation
blogs.description: While hyponatremia is common in SIADH, its subtle extra-neurological manifestations are often missed until complications arise. Using this case as a teaching tool, we highlight persistent hiccups as a specific marker of hypothalamic irritation or severe electrolyte disturbance and discuss the link between profound hyponatremia and rhabdomyolysis (elevated CK). This post serves as a reminder to check electrolytes aggressively in any patient with unexplained hiccups or muscle pain accompanying CNS inflammation.
